newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude sideways unless gasoline falls.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude sideways unless gasoline falls.

text.p: Strength in gasoline futues supported modest moves higher on NYMEX on Thursday but gasoline's upside potential is seen limited today.
Some analysts expect long liquidation if the contract fails to break higher ground, and crude and heating to be pulled down with it.

Tom James, analyst at Credit Lyonais Rouse in Singapore said he expected the market to continue to move sideways with most technical indicators in neutral and trend line support and resistance in place.

"Overall market indicators are in the neutral zone and only gasoline has a limit on it's upside potential, so any drop in prices today will be fundamentally lead, down to pre-Iraq (oil sale) jitters or perhaps some long liquidation in gasoline," James said.
GNI Research said in their daily report that while NYMEX crude managed to close above $19.75 on Thursday its performance was not very convincing.
"We are still rather cautious there is still some work to do to break above $20 and the bulls will have to be pretty brave to get away with that today".
"62.50 is a fairly important number for gasoline and any failure to clear it will spark a profit taking correction that spills into the rest of the complex," they added.

Gasoline has managed to recover from sell-offs holding trendline support back to the middle of June, but while the recent uptrend channel puts resistance around 62.50 cents, recent attempts at breaking it have failed at 62.45. A double top at 62.40 from June 18 and 24 has also shielded it.
The market tackled this 62.50 level in overnight ACCESS trade but was quickly repelled back to around the lows at $61.95.
